Appearance:

sentences.text: ORAL ORDER Mr. Lalit Patel, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has tendered a purshis  stating that the petitioner is pleading guilty and is ready to deposit the fine as per the  direction of this Court.
Mr. K.L. Pandya, learned APP for the State contended that  t h e S t a t e h a s n o o b j e c t i o n i f t h e s a m e i s d i s p o s e d o f b y  imposing appropriate fine.
The said purshis is taken on record.

As such, on going through the records, it is noticed that the offence alleged against the  original accused respondent under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is not  serious in nature and the punishment or penalty prescribed for such offence is not  substantial, and in view of the provisions of Section 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standards  Act, 2006, it is compoundable under Section 69 of the said Act.
In view of the above, this application stands R/CR.RA/173/2015 ORDER d i s p o s e d o f i n t e r m s o f t h e w i t h d r a w a l / c o m p r o m i s e p u r s i s .

The appellant is directed to pay fine of Rs. 25,000/ in the office of the High Court Legal  Gautambhai Maghjibhai Patel vs State Of Gujarat on 22 April, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29817999/
1 Services Committee within a period of four weeks failing which, the matter  s h a l l s t a n d r e v i v e d a u t o m a t i c a l l y .
